scope: Private account-backed recovery for the primary curriculum and assignment editors, including transient session failures discovered during verification

implementation.storage: Migration 010 adds owner-scoped editor_drafts with resource foreign keys. Draft JSON is bounded to a 2 MiB request; at most 20 active copies and 200 total records per account. Copies expire after seven days. Discard removes payload and retains a one-hour tombstone to reject delayed writes; the worker removes up to 500 expired records per maintenance pass.
implementation.authorization: Existing authentication, deleted-profile rejection, trusted gateway checks, CSRF and write rate limits run before the modular drafts handler. Every resource and draft access checks ownership; baseline revisions must exist. Generation snapshots retain their canonical source/task identities and levels.
implementation.ordering: Per-copy sequences reject stale updates. Independent tabs use independent IDs. Discarding a recovered copy checks the sequence so a newer copy from another tab is retained.
implementation.autosave: After a 1.5-second typing pause, with at least five seconds between attempts, save a separate backup rather than a canonical version. Unchanged drafts are not resent. Failed writes require an explicit retry or a newer edit; the UI does not claim a successful backup before acknowledgement.
implementation.recovery: Reopening the same material lists account copies. Restore locks editing while loading, then uses the existing three-way comparison against the current server version. Saving and teacher approval remain explicit actions. Successful canonical save/synchronization clears the owned backup and the recovered copy if it has not advanced elsewhere.
implementation.privacy: The feature writes no document text to localStorage/sessionStorage and captures neither profile forms nor password fields. Workspace editor keys include the authenticated owner. Help and privacy pages describe retention and the boundary for edits not yet acknowledged by the server.
implementation.classFilters: Restore and merge reset curriculum filters and pagination so a changed class cannot hide recovered lessons.
implementation.session: Real traces exposed HTTP 429 on get-session being rendered as a guest page. Only this read endpoint now has a custom 240-request/60-second rule; login/password/plugin rules are unchanged. An initial transient session error presents a localized retry action. Existing session data is retained by the provider during non-401 refresh errors.
implementation.print: Recovery and conflict panels are hidden under print media. A dark-theme logo backing was added after visual inspection.

verification.chromiumFunctionalSuite: 27 passed: server API ownership/CSRF/limits/sequence/tombstones; expiry with a live-copy control; account deletion; reload recovery for both editors; storage refusal; failed autosave/retry; delayed old save versus a new edit; changed-class recovery; existing draft/conflict/password regressions; 40 real session reads; injected 429/503 recovery.
verification.webkitFunctionalSuite: 13 passed after fixing the session issue: reload, conflict, class, delayed-save and session-error cases.
verification.finalPolish: On the final running image, three focused cases passed in each browser: both session-error themes and print suppression of backup/conflict controls. Screenshots were visually inspected; scoped axe and 360px overflow checks passed.
verification.beforeEvidence: The class recovery defect was reproduced on the previous running image: changed class selected but lesson 1 hidden. A real trace showed get-session 429; a fault-injected 429 test also failed before the retry UI was added. Initial WebKit failures were retained as diagnosis, not counted as successful checks.
verification.database: Local migration 010 applied. The real worker removed a deliberately expired synthetic copy while an unexpired control survived. Full isolated PostgreSQL restore verified all public-table content hashes, including 50 editor_drafts records and all ten migrations; see restore.json.
verification.build: Production web and worker images built. Final web build ran all 93 unit tests, type checking, lint and Next.js packaging. The running web image ID matches the final local image tag. Formatting, source visibility, whitespace and secret scans passed.
verification.privacyHTTP: Canonical /privacy returns 200 with both localized draft-retention sections; /privacy/ redirects to it with 308.
verification.ci: All new specifications are included in integration CI. Local results do not claim the newly triggered GitHub run has completed.

remaining: Lite still needs an equivalent recovery/comparison interface.
Last keystrokes before a successful server acknowledgement, offline edits and edits exceeding the request limit are not guaranteed recoverable after a crash.
Measure full-snapshot traffic for large real KTP files, prolonged shared-IP auth traffic and multi-copy management; a forty-read check is not a load test.
Database restore was local; production scheduling, encryption, provider retention and deployment still require the deferred hosting stage. No paid infrastructure or public deployment was started.
The overall product improvement goal remains active.
